newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seven more North Korean defectors arrive in South.
newsitem.headline: Seven more North Korean defectors arrive in South.

text.p: Seven more North Korean asylum seekers have arrived in South Korea through a third country in the latest of a stream of defections, a security official said on Friday.
Two university students and a doctor and his wife were among the seven who were flown in late on Thursday, the official said asking not to be identified.
He said not all the seven were related but declined to give details, citing needs to protect them. State radio said the group arrived via Hong Kong.

"We are not providing detail of the defectors, because we fear they could become targets like Lee Han-young," said the official, referring to a prominent defector who was killed by suspected North Korean hitmen.

Lee, a nephew of North Korean leader Kim Jong-il's former wife, changed his name from Li Il-nam after he defected to the South to cover himself from possible North Korean revenge, but was fatally shot after top Pyongyang ideologue Hwang Jang-yop sought asylum at South Korea's mission in Beijing last month.
Hwang, the most senior North Korean to flee the communist country, is now awaiting departure for Seoul after Beijing sent him to the Philippines last week.
Beijing agonised for more than a month to find a diplomatic solution to Hwang's wishes to go to the South while appearing to save face for its long-time ally North Korea.
Separately on Thursday, a North Korean construction worker from Kuwait, who sought asylum last week at the South Korean mission, arrived in Seoul.
He told reporters he wanted to leave because "there is only death and poverty in North Korea".
In recent month, a string of North Koreans has fled the impoverished North, which is suffering from an acute food shortage.
More than 600 North Korean defectors now live in South Korea and the government is planning to build a camp to house up to 500.
